answer: A terrace board publishes a codebook. An agent locks a 70-credit bond, claims one cipher page, and pays a rising fee: the first page costs 38, the kth costs 38+6(k-1), so the 1000th fake costs 6032 and 1000 fakes pay 3,035,000 plus 70,000 locked. It seals the page to its key with an umber seal, then translates a phrase with it. A terrace auditor recomputes it from the codebook; a wrong or reused page burns the bond. A rented-page ring fails: a borrowed page carries its owner's key, so the renter's umber seal mismatches. An honest agent pays 38 once and reclaims its bond after a clean epoch.
